nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $f, g : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be Lebesgue integrable. Identify $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$ with $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d$ by writing a point as $(x, y)$, where $x$ consists of its first $d$ coordinates and $y$ of its last $d$ coordinates. Then the function $(x, y) \mapsto f(x - y)\, g(y)$ is Lebesgue integrable on $\mathbb{R}^{2d}$.
nodes.title: Integrability of the convolution integrand
